transcript:
Meeting header
Date/Time: 2026-03-07 16:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes (approx)
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Sofia Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Nimbus CTO), Marcus Lee (Nimbus Platform), Dr. Elaine Park (Nimbus Product)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync focusing on reliability follow-ups after yesterday's spike: timeouts and a burst of 5xxs during a billing-run, discussing concurrency limits, backpressure, retry policies and fallback routing to a cheaper model variant. Agreed next steps and owners.

Topics:
- Incident recap (what triggered timeouts/5xxs)
- Concurrency and backpressure knobs (batching, queue depth, circuit breakers)
- Retry semantics and idempotency concerns (client vs server retries)
- Fallback routing and canary strategy (model variants, regional fallback)
- Telemetry gaps and logs needed for deeper postmortem

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everybody, thanks for carving out time. quick agenda: incident recap, what we changed in the last 24 hours, and then tuning + next steps. we have about 55 minutes.
[00:18] Priya Desai: Thanks Alex. yeah, we had a spike in billing job throughput and saw a cluster of timeouts, then some 5xxs following a retry storm. Marcus will walk through exact metrics.
[00:30] Marcus Lee: (sigh) yes, so at 03:12 UTC our batch job scaled up from ~80 rps to 700 rps for 8 minutes, we were hitting request queue saturation on the dedicate pool — sorry, dedicated — the dedicated nodes. latency jumped and a bunch of client-side retries compounded it.
[00:50] Sofia Ramos: Right, was that with your concurrency cap turned off? I think earlier you said you removed the per-worker concurrency limit for throughput.
[01:05] Marcus Lee: We bumped the per-worker concurrency to 32 from 8 to try to push through, that backfired. the runtime's internal batching couldn't keep up, and we saw kv cache thrash — the KV cache, it was basically cold.
[01:22] Dr. Elaine Park: also want to call out we changed the output sampling for a subset of requests during the window which increased average tokens/resp.
[01:35] Alex Kim: ok, perfect. quick clarifying Q: are the retries originating from your side or from a middleware we installed?
[01:45] Priya Desai: majority were client-side - our orchestration retried on 5xx and timeouts, the retry policy had exponential backoff but zero jitter, so retries bunched.
[02:02] Sofia Ramos: zero jitter will absolutely create retry storms. adding jitter plus circuit-breaker style backoff on the client usually helps. on the Redwood side we also have rate limiter and burst window config we can tune.
[02:20] Marcus Lee: can you remind me where to change that limit? is it in the dedicated config or in the console route?
[02:27] Alex Kim: it's in the route settings in the Console — per-model and per-route concurrency and burst size. for Dedicated customers there's also a per-pool queue depth you can tune in the account config. sometimes the UI label says 'burst capacity' but under the hood it maps to queue depth + token-bucket.
[02:45] Priya Desai: got it, we looked at the console after the incident. we also noticed a bunch of 502/503s with the text 'worker unavailable' — is that indicative of overload or something else?
[02:58] Sofia Ramos: usually worker unavailable indicates the worker process dropped or the pool hit OOM and the autoscaler cycled instances. could be load-induced OOMs if tokens per request spiked. also mis-labeled logs sometimes say 'pod restarted' but it's really the runtime restarting.
[03:20] Marcus Lee: we collect pod logs; attaching them in the ticket — you'll see repeated GC/oom lines around the spike.
[03:28] Alex Kim: perfect, please attach. that'll help the postmortem.
[03:34] Priya Desai: what about fallback routing — we have a cheaper 13b model that could handle overflow at lower cost but slightly higher latency. how would that work?
[03:46] Sofia Ramos: good question. we have automatic fallback policies you can configure: route-level fallback to a model variant (e.g., quantized 13b) triggered by a latency threshold or by observed 5xx rate. it can be immediate or gated by a canary percent. in your case I'd suggest a two-step: 1) enable fallback to 13b at 5% immediately, 2) create a canary rollout to 20% with P95 maintenance.
[04:12] Priya Desai: does fallback preserve response structure? our downstream parsers expect a strict schema.
[04:18] Sofia Ramos: yes, you can also configure a response shim or function call map to normalize outputs. sometimes the tokenizer differences require prompt wrappers but we can provide a sample shim.
[04:30] Dr. Elaine Park: small nit — last time the 13b produced slightly different wording that broke our rules engine. how do we validate quality while using fallback?
[04:39] Alex Kim: we recommend running a runsplit eval — send identical requests to both models for a small sample and compare diffs. Redwood Optimize can compute regression metrics for your prompt set. we'll share a guide.
[04:55] Marcus Lee: ok, on retries: should we move to server-side retries only and disable client retries? there's concern about idempotency for some of our calls.
[05:05] Sofia Ramos: generally you want idempotent endpoints and rely on client-side retries with jitter for non-idempotent flows it's tricky. server-side retries can hide issues; also server retries may double-charge tokens if not careful. for POC I'd suggest: make the client add jitter and cap retries to 2, enable server-side short circuit for known transient errors and rely on queue + backpressure rather than blind retries.
[05:30] Priya Desai: token billing concern is huge for us in POC. we don't want accidental huge bills from retries.
[05:37] Alex Kim: noted. we'll provide a config that sets max_retries=2 on client, and server will return 429 when we hit queue saturation which your client can interpret as a signal to backoff more aggressively.
[05:52] Marcus Lee: what's the 429 behavior? currently our clients treat 429 as an immediate retry.
[05:57] Sofia Ramos: default behavior is to treat 429 as throttling: clients should implement exponential backoff with jitter. we can add explicit Retry-After header so clients avoid tight loops. we'll enable that for your routes.
[06:14] Dr. Elaine Park: can Redwood expose token-level cost per route so we can see cost spikes per job?
[06:21] Alex Kim: yes, Console has token-level cost breakdown per route and by model. we'll share a dashboard link and set up a short retention for the POC so you can correlate spikes.
[06:34] Priya Desai: thanks. telemetry — we still have some blind spots, like missing correlation IDs in some traces.
[06:41] Sofia Ramos: include a Correlation-ID header on requests; Redwood will pass that through to logs. also enable tracing hooks — we can provide an example for OpenTelemetry shim.
[06:54] Marcus Lee: we'll add the header starting this afternoon.
[06:58] Alex Kim: good. next I want to talk about concurrency knobs: we can limit per-route concurrency, set max inflight per-worker, adjust batch size and max tokens per batch. changing batch size affects latency/cost tradeoffs.
[07:15] Marcus Lee: can you remind us recommended defaults for a Dedicated 8-GPU pool?
[07:22] Sofia Ramos: for a Dedicated 8-GPU pool running 70B-ish workloads we usually set per-worker concurrency to 8-12 for stable latency, batching of up to 4-8 requests depending on avg seq length, and queue depth of ~200 for burst tolerance. for quantized 13b you can push concurrency higher.
[07:40] Priya Desai: in our case many requests are short (avg 60 tokens) but a subset is 600-800 tokens which drove the OOM. can we have request-size-aware routing?
[07:50] Sofia Ramos: yes — route by metadata: short/long payload classification. we often suggest tagging long requests as a separate route with lower concurrency and larger batch timeout. that avoids blocking short reqs.
[08:04] Dr. Elaine Park: that sounds promising. what about our billing job which is bursty but short — how should we handle?
[08:12] Alex Kim: for bursty short jobs, use a dedicated route with a higher burst window and shorter max tokens per request; also enable prefix caching for repeated prompts so repeated tokens are cached.
[08:24] Marcus Lee: prefix cache, we saw 'kv cash miss' in the logs earlier — is there an auto-warm mechanism?
[08:32] Sofia Ramos: not automatic across restarts; you can pre-warm the KV cache by hitting warmup endpoints or sending synthetic warm requests. we can provide a warmup script.
[08:45] Priya Desai: please share that script.
[08:48] Alex Kim: will do.
[08:51] [09:00] (short silence as team reviews shared slides)
[09:10] Marcus Lee: question around autoscaling — our Dedicated pool scaled but lags by 30-45s, that's the gap that caused the OOMs. any improvements?
[09:21] Sofia Ramos: autoscaler tuning is a balance. we can reduce scale-up cool-down and add predictive policies based on schedule (if you know the billing job occurs at X) so the pool pre-provisions. also consider reserved burst capacity if jobs are predictable.
[09:37] Priya Desai: we can reserve a small burst capacity for nightly runs. what's the cost hit?
[09:44] Alex Kim: small — reserved burst is billed at a lower incremental rate than full reserved GPUs; we'll send a cost estimate.
[09:51] Marcus Lee: ok. on the subject of 5xxs: are there any runtime flags you recommend to reduce 5xx on overload?
[09:59] Sofia Ramos: enable early rejection thresholds so requests that exceed queue depth get 429 quickly; enable adaptive batching throttle to shrink batch size under load; and use circuit breaker to shed load rather than let the runtime OOM.
[10:15] Dr. Elaine Park: can we do end-to-end tests simulating the 700 rps burst?
[10:20] Alex Kim: yes, we'll hand over a load harness and a sandbox account; run a 1k concurrent request test against the POC route with the suggested configs and report results.
[10:29] Marcus Lee: what's recommended concurrency for the load harness? do you mean real concurrent connections or RPS?
[10:34] Sofia Ramos: both. do a 1k concurrent connections with a poisson arrival pattern peaking at 700 rps for 10 minutes to reproduce the incident. we'll include sample scripts for JMeter/k6.
[10:47] Priya Desai: perfect. next, the 5xxs included some 'model compilation error' messages — could that be from quantization or kernel selection?
[10:57] Sofia Ramos: "model compilation error" often stems from a kernel mismatch for a specific sequence length or a quant path hitting an unsupported op. we saw this when we tested the latest quantized build last week — sometimes a fallback to the FP16 path helps. we'll check the model logs.
[11:15] Marcus Lee: can you attach those model-compile logs? our SRE needs them for the ticket.
[11:21] Alex Kim: yes — we'll gather and upload.
[11:24] Priya Desai: security question — will enabling fallback to 13b route data to a different region or vendor? we need to ensure PHI stays in-region.
[11:35] Sofia Ramos: fallback can be constrained by region and tenancy. for Nimbus Health we'll ensure fallback stays within your VPC / region; for hosted fallback we can limit to redwood-dedicated within region. we'll add an explicit region-bound routing rule.
[11:52] Dr. Elaine Park: and audit logs for those fallbacks? we need clear traces of which model served which request.
[11:58] Alex Kim: Console stores model-level request metadata and we can export audit logs to your S3/KMS. we'll add retention and export plan for the POC.
[12:12] Marcus Lee: on observability, we need more granular error codes — the 5xx in logs are generic. can you push more specific error tagging?
[12:22] Sofia Ramos: yes we can bump the verbosity for POC routes to include subcodes (OOM, COMPILATION_ERROR, WORKER_DROP). we'll flip that on for your routes. note higher verbosity increases log volume.
[12:35] Priya Desai: fine for POC window.
[12:39] Alex Kim: moving on to concrete tuning we'll propose: per-route concurrency cap 12, max inflight per-worker 24, queue depth 250, add Retry-After header on 429, enable jittered client retries max 2, fallback to 13b at 5% then canary to 20% — any objections?
[12:59] Marcus Lee: sounds good. can we make the fallback threshold configurable by P95 latency instead of 5xx count?
[13:05] Sofia Ramos: absolutely — can tie fallback to P95 > X ms or 5xx rate. we'll include both in the sample config.
[13:15] Dr. Elaine Park: for quality gating, can Redwood Optimize run diffs on a 500-sample set?
[13:21] Alex Kim: yes, Redwood Optimize supports pairwise diffs and will flag regressions; we'll run that for you if you provide the prompt set.
[13:32] Marcus Lee: timeline? we need the config and scripts by Tuesday.
[13:36] Alex Kim: we'll target 2026-03-10 for configs and load scripts. SEs will run the batching/kv warmup tests by 2026-03-11.
[13:46] Priya Desai: ok. anything else on the incident root cause?
[13:50] Sofia Ramos: primary drivers were sudden burst, zero-jitter client retries, and mixed payload sizes causing memory pressure. secondary was autoscaler lag. we'll capture that in the postmortem.
[14:05] Marcus Lee: agreed. for the postmortem can Redwood include suggested client retry pseudocode? that'll help our engs implement jitter properly.
[14:12] Alex Kim: yes. we'll include example JS/Python clients with exponential backoff + jitter + idempotency key pattern.
[14:21] Dr. Elaine Park: will you also share the warmup script?
[14:24] Sofia Ramos: yes — warmup script, load harness, and sample configs.
[14:28] [14:40] (file links shared in chat: POC-benchmarks.xlsx, warmup.sh, load-harness-k6.js, security-whitepaper.pdf)
[14:45] Marcus Lee: we have a procurement checkpoint next week; any impact on procurement docs from enabling fallback?
[14:52] Alex Kim: no, but we'll include a note in the docs that fallback is region-restricted and audit-logged. procurement should be fine.
[14:59] Priya Desai: last Q — any recommendation for alert thresholds to catch this earlier?
[15:05] Sofia Ramos: alert on sudden delta on inflight (>200% over baseline in 1m), queue depth > 70% for >1m, P95 spike beyond baseline + 2x for >3m, and 5xx rate > 1% sustained for 5m. also watch for correlated token-cost spikes.
[15:25] Marcus Lee: we'll set up those alerts.
[15:29] Alex Kim: recap and owners — action items listed in the doc: configs and scripts by 2026-03-10 (Alex/Sofia), KV warmup tests by 2026-03-11 (Sofia), customer to run load harness and share traffic profile by 2026-03-12 (Marcus). follow-up canary meeting on 2026-03-15.
[15:48] Priya Desai: sounds good. thanks team.
[15:53] Dr. Elaine Park: thanks.
[15:55] Alex Kim: thanks everyone, we'll upload artifacts and notes. talk soon.

End of transcript.
